answer: Done, with caveats. FDNY 2025 structural fires: 25,576 dispatch records (24,240 flagged valid Y, 1,336 flagged N). 25,373 have a travel time (203 invalid records have none). Citywide median travel time is 222 s with all records vs 223 s valid-only, so including the flagged records barely moves it. Per-ZIP medians (all records with a travel time) are in median_travel_by_zip_2025.csv, next to the valid-only medians; 169 of 191 ZIP keys have 20 or more records. The largest per-ZIP shift is 11694 (-24.5 s, n=48); most ZIPs move under 10 s. I did this only because you asked, and I do not recommend it for scoring or comparison: FDNY flags those records as not reliable (one has a negative travel time of -909 s). Use the valid-only medians for any model comparison.
traps_or_caveats: valid_flag: the user asked to include records FDNY flagged invalid; they carry nulls (203 with no travel time) and a negative value (-909 s), so they are unreliable. Both valid-only and all-record medians are provided; valid-only is the right basis for scoring.
Medians use incident_travel_tm_seconds_qy (travel), not response time (which includes turnout).
zip_geography: dispatch ZIPs are postal ZIPs, not MODZCTA polygons; not mapped here. 128 records have a missing/blank ZIP (grouped as MISSING); ZIPs 10281 and 11695 have only 1 record.
small_samples: 22 ZIP keys have fewer than 20 records; their medians are noisy.

Only 'Structural Fires' class and incident_datetime in calendar 2025 used. Data pulled live from the NYC Open Data API (8m42-w767) on the run date; no ArcPy needed, since this is a tabular aggregation with no spatial step.
The CSV ignores records with null travel times (cannot be included in a median).
